# FDG8005

> DO name custom attribute classes with the suffix “Attribute.”

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.2 Attributes.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1710
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Test profile: none, because CA1710 also enforces the other suffixes of Table 3-5, and chapter 3 is off in the test profile. CA1710 reports a class derived directly from System.Attribute whose name does not end with Attribute; with its default dotnet_code_quality.CA1710.exclude_indirect_base_types = true it does not report an attribute derived from another attribute class (probe with SDK 10.0.402), so coverage is partial. FDG3049 in chapter 3 is the same guideline. Renaming a public type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1710 has no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
public class ObsoleteAttribute : Attribute { ... }
```
